name: HQ-17 short-range air-defence system
overview_md:
The HQ-17 is the PLA's modern short-range, point-defence surface-to-air missile system — the inner layer of Chinese air defence that protects manoeuvre forces and high-value assets from aircraft, helicopters, cruise missiles, precision-guided munitions and, increasingly, drones. Derived from the Russian Tor-M1, it has been developed into an indigenous Chinese system on both tracked and wheeled (HQ-17A) chassis.

Where the HQ-9 and HQ-16 provide long- and medium-range area defence, the HQ-17 fills the close-in gap: a fast-reacting, vertically-launched system that travels with armoured and mechanised columns and engages low-flying, agile threats at ranges of around 15 km and altitudes up to roughly 10 km. Its quick reaction time and ability to engage on the move make it well suited to defeating the precision strikes and loitering munitions that increasingly threaten ground forces.

For an analyst, the HQ-17 is the layer that makes Chinese ground formations survivable under air attack. As drones and cruise missiles proliferate — vividly demonstrated in recent conflicts — short-range mobile air defence has become essential, and the HQ-17 (with related gun-missile systems) is how the PLA keeps its armoured spearheads protected while the HQ-16 and HQ-9 handle the medium and long tiers above it.

additional.targets: Aircraft, helicopters, cruise missiles, PGMs, UAVs
additional.feature: Fast reaction; engages low/agile threats with manoeuvre forces

builder: China Aerospace Science and Industry Corp. (CASIC)

combat_history.event: No confirmed combat; fielded with PLA combined-arms brigades and exercised in air-defence drills.

modernization.description: Improved sensors and engagement against small drones and loitering munitions.
modernization.impact: Keeps manoeuvre forces survivable against proliferating drone threats.

vulnerabilities.description: Point-defence range only; not an area defender.
Expensive interceptors versus swarms of cheap UAS.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Pairing with gun systems and EW.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Mobile point defence accompanying armoured/mechanised forces and protecting key assets.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Inner layer beneath HQ-16 and HQ-9 in the IADS.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Widely fielded on tracked and wheeled chassis.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The HQ-17 derives from the Russian Tor and is China's indigenised short-range point-defence SAM.
The HQ-16 is the medium tier; the HQ-17 is the close-in point-defence layer.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The inner layers of Chinese air defence.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Pantsir combines guns and missiles for point defence; the HQ-17 is missile-only.

doctrine.role: Short-range point-defence SAM protecting manoeuvre forces and key assets from close-in air threats.
doctrine.employment: Fast-reacting vertical-launch engagement of low, agile threats while accompanying ground columns.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Mobile, quick-reaction close defence — the inner layer of the IADS.
doctrine.threat_context: Keeps PLA armoured spearheads survivable against PGMs, cruise missiles and drones.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the Russian Tor (parent), the HQ-16 (above) and the Pantsir.
